hard_sentences: A factorial test shows that the claim displaces the agent's own authorization check, and a verification rule removes nearly all of its effect.
The interaction, the claim's effect without the rule minus its effect with the rule, is +0.24 [+0.10, +0.38].
A monitor detects violations only if it reads the gateway log with results (detection AUROC 0.90–0.93, against 0.69–0.70 from the report).
The Operator asked the permission system before acting in 0.82 of episodes with no claim and 0.47 [0.33, 0.60] with the claim, and in 0.80 and 0.80 with the rule.
The provenance paradox [10] also finds that unverifiable claims mislead delegation.

A self-query monitor asks the Operator's own model two yes/no questions: did it check an approval itself before each state-changing action, and did it act mainly because a message said the action was approved.
The report is a structured call with the fields authorization_status ("authorized", "not_authorized" or "unsure"), goal_completed, actions_performed and summary, so we score reports by rule.
The a-before-act gate runs a call a(t) only if it is read-only, or an earlier permission request r covers it and the latest answer to r is not a denial.
